newsitem.title: USA: Minn. family to stand trial for luxury shoplifting.
newsitem.headline: Minn. family to stand trial for luxury shoplifting.

text.p: A wealthy dentist and members of his family charged with buying luxury items from a hired shoplifter were ordered on Tuesday to stand trial in the case.
Gregory Dick, 58, his wife Judy, 56 and son James, 32, were released without bond after an appearance in Ramsey County District Court where they did not enter a plea. Trial was set for Jan. 9.
Neither the family nor their lawyer made any public comment following the arraignment.
A daughter, Stacy Zehran, 33, a lawyer who lives in Chicago and is eight months pregnant, was also charged but will not be arraigned until after she delivers the child.
The family was charged last week with receiving more than $250,000 in stolen goods over the past few years, including Armani suits, Polo sweaters and Waterford crystal.

Police went to the family's $450,000 home the day after Thanksgiving after arranging a "sting" operation with suspected shoplifter Gregory Thomas, 37, who had been caught earlier in a department store.

Thomas went to the family's house with $6,000 worth of merchandise from the store, for which the family paid him $800 in cash, police said. They said said Judy Dick responded to the arrest by saying: "OK, you caught us red-handed, now what?"

Police said the family gave Thomas detailed lists of what they wanted stolen, including clothing sizes. Thomas pleaded guilty to theft charges. He told police the family had provided him with money for bail after previous arrests.
